identity.title: Forced expiratory time >6-9 s (stethoscope over trachea, full forced exhalation)

technique.how: Place the stethoscope diaphragm over the trachea in the suprasternal notch. Ask the patient to take a maximal breath in and blow out as hard and fast as possible with the mouth open until no more air comes; time with a second hand from the start of exhalation until airflow noise stops. Take the best of two or three efforts.
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to cooperate with a maximal effort; not in severe distress.
technique.contraindications: Recent pneumothorax, haemoptysis, or unstable chest wall/abdominal wounds where a forced manoeuvre is unsafe (relative).

interpretation.positive_finding: In patients referred for spirometry aged >=60, an FET >8 s raises the likelihood of obstructive airways disease about four-fold (LR 4.08, 95% CI 2.54-6.79); 6-8 s roughly doubles it (LR 2.19).
interpretation.negative_finding: An FET of 4-6 s lowers the likelihood of obstruction in patients >=60 (LR 0.42, 95% CI 0.24-0.73); the test discriminates less well in younger subjects, so a short FET does not exclude asthma in the young.
interpretation.pitfalls: Submaximal effort, cough, or stopping early shortens the time; glottic closure or a slow start lengthens it. Sensitivity/specificity depend on the cutoff, and the original study's optimal cutoff was 6 s, which differs from the '>6-9 s' range in this id's title.
interpretation.changes_what: Long FET (>8 s): treat as probable obstruction and confirm with spirometry/peak flow. Short FET (4-6 s) in an older patient: obstruction less likely, look for other causes of dyspnea.

estimates.target_condition: Obstructive airways disease on spirometry; finding = FET greater than 8 seconds (stratum LR), patients aged >=60
estimates.population: Consecutive patients referred to a tertiary-hospital pulmonary function laboratory (preoperative, acute/chronic and occupational lung disease), n=400; FET measured by a physician examiner; stratum LRs from age-adjusted logistic model, subjects aged >=60 years
estimates.reference_standard: Spirometry (obstructive airways disease by laboratory criteria)
estimates.quote: of greater than 8 seconds, 4.08 (95% CI, 2.54 to 6.79)

estimates.target_condition: Obstructive airways disease on spirometry; finding = FET 6 to 8 seconds (stratum LR), patients aged >=60
estimates.population: Consecutive patients referred to a tertiary-hospital pulmonary function laboratory (preoperative, acute/chronic and occupational lung disease), n=400; FET measured by a physician examiner; stratum LRs from age-adjusted logistic model, subjects aged >=60 years
estimates.reference_standard: Spirometry (obstructive airways disease by laboratory criteria)

estimates.target_condition: Obstructive airways disease on spirometry; finding = FET 4 to 6 seconds (stratum LR <1, i.e. this band argues AGAINST obstruction), patients aged >=60
estimates.population: Consecutive patients referred to a tertiary-hospital pulmonary function laboratory (preoperative, acute/chronic and occupational lung disease), n=400; FET measured by a physician examiner; stratum LRs from age-adjusted logistic model, subjects aged >=60 years
estimates.reference_standard: Spirometry (obstructive airways disease by laboratory criteria)
estimates.quote: an FET of 4 to 6 seconds is 0.42 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.24 to 0.73)

sources.citation: Schapira RM, Schapira MM, Funahashi A, McAuliffe TL, Varkey B. The value of the forced expiratory time in the physical diagnosis of obstructive airways disease. JAMA. 1993;270(6):731-736.
Holleman DR Jr, Simel DL. Does the clinical examination predict airflow limitation? JAMA. 1995;273(4):313-319.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use in an exhausted, hypoxic or severely distressed patient, or to decide against bronchodilators in an acute wheezy presentation.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: A patient too breathless to perform a forced exhalation is showing a severity sign; act on that rather than on the timing.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Interexaminer agreement moderate-good: quote 'The kappa statistic for interexaminer agreement is 0.70.' (Schapira 1993, Abstract, Results; 100 subjects examined by pairs of physicians).

extraction_notes: Anchor RCE PMID 7815660 confirmed (title matches) but has no PubMed abstract and no PMC text, so its pooled FET summary could not be read; the primary study it draws on (Schapira 1993, PMID 8336375, confirmed) supplies all numbers from its abstract. Schapira reports multilevel stratum LRs by FET band (4-6 s, 6-8 s, >8 s) for subjects >=60, not a single LR+/LR- pair; each band is entered as a separate estimate with the value in lr_positive (the LR for that band being present), and the 4-6 s band with LR 0.42 is explicitly labelled as arguing against obstruction. Sensitivity/specificity at each cutoff (2-14 s) are in the full text, not the abstract, so they are null. Quote 'Using the FET maneuver with a cutoff value of 6 seconds will correctly diagnose the greatest number of subjects' (Abstract). Status partially_quantified because no estimate has a sens/spec pair or an LR+/LR- pair, and the id's '>6-9 s' threshold differs from the study's bands. CARE-COAD1 (Straus 2000, PMID 10770147) was fetched but does not evaluate FET.
